questions.question: What is the mean annual average temperature (in degrees Celsius) in 'Temperate' vegetation zones?
questions.questionHtml: What is the mean annual average temperature (in degrees Celsius) in 'Temperate' vegetation zones?
questions.solution:
Key Points

  • The mean annual average temperature in 'Temperate' vegetation zones is 7°C to 17°C.
  • Temperate zones are characterized by their moderate weather conditions, falling between the polar and tropical zones.
  • These regions experience four distinct seasons: winter, spring, summer, and autumn.
  • Vegetation in temperate zones includes deciduous forests, grasslands, and temperate rainforests.

Additional Information

  • Temperate zones are located between the tropics and the polar regions, typically between 30° and 60° latitude in both hemispheres.
  • The climate and ecosystem diversity in temperate zones support a wide range of plant and animal life, adapted to seasonal changes.
  • Human activities, including agriculture, urbanization, and industrialization, have significantly impacted many temperate ecosystems.
  • Conservation efforts in temperate regions aim to protect natural habitats and biodiversity while managing sustainable use of resources.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the characteristics of tropical cyclones?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT the characteristics of tropical cyclones?

options.text: It is a low-pressure area surrounded by increasing high-pressure isobars.
options.html: It is a low-pressure area surrounded by increasing high-pressure isobars.

options.text: The eyewall is having strong winds and torrential rains.
options.html: The eyewall is having strong winds and torrential rains.

options.text: Within the cyclone, winds move clockwise in the northern hemisphere and anti-clockwise in the southern hemisphere.
options.html: Within the cyclone, winds move clockwise in the northern hemisphere and anti-clockwise in the southern hemisphere.

options.text: It developed in summer season in the vicinity of Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone.
options.html: It developed in summer season in the vicinity of Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone.

questions.solution:
Option 3 is NOT correct.

Tropical cyclones developed in the region between Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn.

  • Tropical cyclones are usually developed in summer season in the area of Inter Tropical Convergence Zone over warm ocean surfaces.
  • A tropical cyclone is like a heat engine which is energized by the latent heat of condensation.
  • Generally, it is formed due to low pressure of thermal origin. Some of the conditions favouring forming of tropical cyclones are,
    • Large sea surface with a temperature higher than 27-degree Celsius and presence of Coriolis force.
    • Weak low-pressure area or low level of cyclonic circulations.
  • A cyclone has a central cloud known as ‘eye’ of the cyclone with a diameter of 10-50 km.
    • The eye is the lowest surface area composed of subsiding and warm air.
  • The eye is surrounded by wall cloud region or ‘eyewall’.
    • It is a circular rotating region of intense thunderstorms up to 15 km of height.
    • The eyewall has very strong winds and torrential rains.
  • After the eyewall, one or more spiral branches or rainbands may radiate having cumulus and cumulonimbus clouds.
  • The vertical extent of the cyclone is about 15 km and diameter may range 80 to 300 km.
  • Within the cyclone, the winds move anti-clockwise in the northern hemisphere and clockwise in the southern hemisphere. Hence, Option 3 is NOT correct.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct description of the term 'Cold Front' with reference to the atmosphere?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the correct description of the term 'Cold Front' with reference to the atmosphere?

options.text: It is a transition zone in the atmosphere where an advancing cold air mass displaces a warm air mass.
options.html: It is a transition zone in the atmosphere where an advancing cold air mass displaces a warm air mass.

options.text: It is a transition zone in the atmosphere where a warm air mass displaces a cold air mass.
options.html: It is a transition zone in the atmosphere where a warm air mass displaces a cold air mass.

options.text: It is a transition zone in the atmosphere where a hot air mass displaces a cold air mass.
options.html: It is a transition zone in the atmosphere where a hot air mass displaces a cold air mass.

options.text: It is a transition zone in the atmosphere where a cold air mass turns into the cloud.
options.html: It is a transition zone in the atmosphere where a cold air mass turns into the cloud.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is It is a transition zone in the atmosphere where an advancing cold air mass displaces a warm air mass..

Key Points

  • A cold front is the leading edge of a cold air mass that replaces a warmer air mass, often resulting in abrupt weather changes such as thunderstorms or heavy rain.
  • When a cold front moves into a region, it forces the warm, moist air ahead of it to rise rapidly, causing condensation and the formation of clouds and precipitation.
  • Cold fronts are typically associated with strong winds, a drop in temperature, and sometimes severe weather conditions like hail or even tornadoes.
  • They are represented by blue lines with triangles on weather maps, with the triangles pointing in the direction of the front's movement.
  • Cold fronts often bring a significant change in weather, with cooler, drier air following behind the front.

Additional Information

  • It is a transition zone in the atmosphere where a warm air mass displaces a cold air mass
    • This refers to a warm front, which occurs when a warm air mass moves over a cold air mass.
    • Warm fronts are characterized by gradual lifting of warm air, forming extensive cloud cover and often resulting in prolonged, steady rain or drizzle.
  •  Cold Fronts and their Effects
    • Cold fronts are a crucial component of mid-latitude cyclones and often result in abrupt weather transitions.
    • They are associated with intense weather phenomena, including thunderstorms, heavy precipitation, and temperature drops.
    • Understanding cold fronts is essential for weather forecasting and predicting severe weather events.

questions.question: Which of the following languages is suitable for artificial intelligence?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following languages is suitable for artificial intelligence?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer: Prolog is a general-purpose programming language associated with artificial intelligence and computational linguistics.

  • All of the listed languages can be used to implement some form of AI, but each one is suitable for different aspects of AI.

Key Points

  • Fortran: It's an old language typically used for numerical and scientific computing. It's not commonly used for modern AI applications but can still be used if necessary, especially for tasks that require heavy numerical computations.
  • Basic: It's a beginner-friendly language. Though it's not typically used for AI applications due to the lack of advanced data structures and libraries, it can be used to implement simple AI systems.
  • Prolog: It's a logic programming language often associated with AI, especially in the domain of expert systems, natural language processing, and knowledge representation. It supports pattern matching and automatic backtracking, which are powerful for these types of tasks.
  • 'C': It's a low-level, general-purpose language. It can be used for AI development, but it might not be the most efficient choice. It lacks the high-level abstractions and libraries (such as TensorFlow or PyTorch) that Python provides, which are commonly used in AI.

Out of these options, Prolog is likely the most directly associated with AI.

Additional InformationHowever, it should be noted that in current AI development, Python is by far the most widely used language due to its simplicity, flexibility, and the broad ecosystem of AI and machine learning libraries available. Other languages like Java, R, and Julia are also often used.

questions.question: Who said "We are also humans" in the Chawdar Talab Satyagraha?
questions.questionHtml: Who said "We are also humans" in the Chawdar Talab Satyagraha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.

Key Points

  • Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, a key figure in India's social justice movement, made the statement "We are also humans" during the Chawdar Talab Satyagraha.
  • The Chawdar Talab Satyagraha (Mahad Satyagraha), led by Dr. Ambedkar in 1927, was a landmark protest aimed at asserting the right of the Dalits (then referred to as "untouchables") to access public water resources.
  • It was held at the Chawdar Tank in Mahad, Maharashtra, where Dalits were prohibited from drinking water despite the tank being public property.
  • Dr. Ambedkar's leadership in the movement symbolized the fight against caste-based discrimination and advocated for the principles of equality and human dignity.
  • The Satyagraha is remembered as a historic step in the Dalit emancipation movement and a pivotal point in India's struggle for social justice.

Additional Information

  • Swami Sahajanand:
    • Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was a prominent Indian freedom fighter and peasant leader.
    • He played a significant role in the Indian independence movement and is remembered for championing the rights of farmers and laborers.
    • His work focused on the abolition of feudal practices and empowering the agrarian community.
  • Mahatma Gandhi:
    • Mahatma Gandhi, the father of the nation, led several movements in India based on non-violence and truth, such as the Salt Satyagraha and the Quit India Movement.
    • While Gandhi worked extensively for the upliftment of Dalits (whom he referred to as "Harijans"), he was not directly associated with the Chawdar Talab Satyagraha.
    • Gandhi's efforts focused on eradicating untouchability and promoting communal harmony.
  • M. C. Raja:
    • M. C. Raja (Muttaiya Chidambaram Pillai Raja) was a prominent Dalit leader from Tamil Nadu.
    • He was active in politics and worked for the social and economic upliftment of the Dalit community.
    • He played an important role in advocating for Dalit rights but was not associated with the Chawdar Talab Satyagraha.

questions.question: Which of the following is the non-metallic form of mineral?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the non-metallic form of  mineral?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Mica". 

Key Points

The inorganic materials that are found naturally as minerals. They can be found in a variety of settings. Crystalline structures and specific chemical compositions are characteristics of minerals.

  • Metallic minerals are those that contain metals in their natural state.

    • Examples of metallic minerals include bauxite, gold, silver, copper, and iron.

  • Minerals without any metal content are referred to as non-metallic minerals.

    • When non-metallic minerals are liquefied, nothing new can be made from them, making them a unique class of chemical elements.

    • Minerals like limestone, mica and gypsum, coal, and petroleum are examples of non-metallic minerals.

    • Inorganic, non-metallic silicate makes up the majority of mica's chemical makeup.

questions.question: Statement 1: In Newton’s equilibrium theory, the centrifugal force generated by the Earth-moon system plays a significant role in creating tidal bulges. Statement 2: The tidal bulges predicted by this theory are stationary and do not move with the Earth’s rotation.
questions.questionHtml:
Statement 1: In Newton’s equilibrium theory, the centrifugal force generated by the Earth-moon system plays a significant role in creating tidal bulges.

Statement 2: The tidal bulges predicted by this theory are stationary and do not move with the Earth’s rotation.

options.text: Statement 1 is False, but Statement 2 is True
options.html: Statement 1 is False, but Statement 2 is True

options.text: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false.
options.html: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false.

Key Points

Statement 1: In Newton’s equilibrium theory, the centrifugal force generated by the Earth-moon system plays a significant role in creating tidal bulges is true because,-

  • Equilibrium Theory: Newton’s equilibrium theory describes the gravitational interactions between Earth, the moon, and the sun, which cause tides.
  • Gravitational Forces: The gravitational pull of the moon primarily, and to a lesser extent of the sun, creates tidal forces that cause the water to bulge out on the side of Earth closest to the moon and the side farthest from the moon.
  • Centrifugal Force: The Earth and moon orbit around a common center of mass, and this orbital motion generates a centrifugal force, which is most pronounced on the side of Earth opposite the moon.
  • The combination of the moon’s gravitational pull and the centrifugal force created by this movement results in the formation of two tidal bulges on opposite sides of the Earth.
  • These tidal bulges lead to high tides in the regions of the Earth beneath the bulges.

Statement 2: The tidal bulges predicted by this theory are stationary and do not move with the Earth’s rotation is false because,-

  • Tidal Movement: In reality, the tidal bulges move along with the Earth’s rotation. As the Earth rotates, different areas pass through the tidal bulges, causing the observed rise and fall of sea levels.
  • Dynamic Nature: The equilibrium theory assumes that the tidal bulges are fixed relative to the positions of the moon and sun, but due to Earth’s rotation and gravitational interactions, these bulges travel westward with the Earth's rotation.
  • Local Geographies: The actual movement of tidal bulges is also influenced by the shape of ocean basins, coastlines, and the Coriolis effect, which cause variations in tidal patterns around the globe.
  • Tidal Cycles: This rotation leads to the regular cycles of high and low tides experienced along coastlines approximately twice each day.

Additional Information

  • Dynamic Theory of Tides: Unlike Newton’s equilibrium theory, the dynamic theory of tides considers the effects of the Earth’s rotation, the geometry of ocean basins, and frictional forces.
  • This dynamic theory provides a more accurate representation of tidal movements by taking into account the fluid dynamics of ocean water.
  • Real-World Tides: Tides are also influenced by meteorological conditions such as wind and atmospheric pressure, which can enhance or diminish tidal effects in certain regions.
  • Understanding the interaction of multiple forces and dynamic conditions is key to accurately predicting and explaining tidal behaviors observed in different parts of the world.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Rowlatt Act, which was introduced by the British government to curb political dissent in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Rowlatt Act, which was introduced by the British government to curb political dissent in India?

options.text: Arrest of political leaders without warrants
options.html: Arrest of political leaders without warrants

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Restrictions on freedom of expression.

Key Points

  • The Rowlatt Act, officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919, was enacted by the British government in India to suppress political dissent and revolutionary activities.
  • It allowed the government to arrest individuals suspected of revolutionary activities without providing a warrant and detain them without trial for an indefinite period, which was a direct violation of basic human rights.
  • One of the provisions included the censorship of the press, aimed at curbing the dissemination of anti-government information and revolutionary ideas.
  • The act gave authorities the power to arrest political leaders and activists without requiring a warrant, which undermined legal safeguards for individuals.
  • The provision of "arrest without trial" was one of the most controversial aspects, as it denied individuals the right to a fair trial, violating the principles of justice.
  • However, the act did not explicitly include any clause that imposed "restrictions on freedom of expression". Although censorship of the press indirectly affected freedom of expression, the act did not target this right specifically as a provision.
  • This act faced widespread protests across India, including the famous Jallianwala Bagh massacre, which occurred as a result of public agitation against the act.

Additional Information

  • Censorship of press
    • The Rowlatt Act imposed censorship on the press to suppress revolutionary ideas and anti-government sentiments.
    • Under this provision, newspapers and publications were monitored, and any content deemed inflammatory or against British rule was censored.
    • This restriction was aimed at controlling public opinion and preventing the spread of nationalist ideas.
  • Arrest of political leaders without warrants
    • One of the most criticized provisions of the Rowlatt Act was the authority given to the police to arrest political leaders and activists without requiring a warrant.
    • This provision enabled arbitrary arrests, targeting prominent leaders involved in the freedom struggle.
  • Arrest without trial
    • The act allowed detention without trial, meaning individuals could be imprisoned indefinitely without being formally charged or given a chance to defend themselves in court.
    • This provision violated fundamental judicial principles and sparked widespread outrage among Indians.

questions.question: The Southern Oscillation is a seesaw pattern between which of these two oceans?
questions.questionHtml: The Southern Oscillation is a seesaw pattern between which of these two oceans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

  • The Southern Oscillation refers to the seesaw pattern of atmospheric pressure that occurs between the western and eastern Pacific Ocean regions.
    • This phenomenon is closely linked to El Niño and La Niña events.
    • The Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) measures the difference in air pressure between Tahiti (in the eastern Pacific) and Darwin (in the western Pacific).
    • El Niño and La Niña are the warm and cold phases of this oscillation, which affects global weather patterns, including those in the Indian Ocean. Hence, option 2 is correct.

Additional Information

Southern Oscillation:

  • The Southern Oscillation (SO) is a natural climate phenomenon that describes the periodic fluctuation in atmospheric pressure over the tropical Indian and Pacific Oceans.
  • It is an integral component of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycle, which is a major driver of climate variability globally.
  • The Southern Oscillation is the see-saw pattern between high pressure in the eastern Pacific and low pressure in the western Pacific, which occurs every 2 to 7 years.
  • It is directly related to El Niño (warming of ocean temperatures) and La Niña (cooling of ocean temperatures).

How the Southern Oscillation Affects Weather Patterns:

  • El Niño (Warm Phase):
    • High pressure in the western Pacific (Indian Ocean and Indonesia).
    • Low pressure in the eastern Pacific (off the coast of South America).
    • Global Effects:
    • Droughts in the Indian subcontinent and Australia.
    • Heavy rains and flooding in the western coast of South America.
    • Disruption of monsoon patterns in India and Southeast Asia.
  • La Niña (Cool Phase):
    • The pressure pattern reverses, leading to:
    • Increased rainfall in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
    • Drier conditions in South America.
    • Cooler sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific.

Key Impact on India and Surrounding Regions:

  • The Southern Oscillation is crucial in determining the Indian Monsoon and can lead to either excessive rainfall or drought conditions depending on the phase of the oscillation.
  • For example, El Niño years often correspond with weak monsoon seasons, leading to water scarcity and crop failures in India.

Interconnectedness of Oceans:

  • Pacific Ocean: The eastern side of the Pacific (off the coast of South America) experiences a cooling or warming phase depending on the Southern Oscillation, directly impacting global weather.
  • Indian Ocean: The change in the pressure pattern of the Southern Oscillation affects the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), which can influence the Indian Monsoon and weather patterns in Southeast Asia.

questions.question: Which language recently received "Classical Language" status at the national level?
questions.questionHtml: Which language recently received "Classical Language" status at the national level?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Marathi.

Key Points

  • Marathi was recently granted the status of a "Classical Language" at the national level in India.
  • A language is designated as a Classical Language when it meets certain criteria such as being of great antiquity, having a rich literary tradition, and being distinct from modern languages.
  • The recognition as a Classical Language brings several benefits, including financial assistance for the development of the language and its literature.
  • Marathi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly in the Indian state of Maharashtra.
  • It is one of the 22 scheduled languages of India as per the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
  • The language has a long and rich history, with written records dating back to around the 11th century.
  • Marathi literature is known for its diverse forms of poetry, prose, and drama.
  • The recognition is expected to further encourage the preservation, study, and promotion of Marathi culture and heritage.

Additional Information

  • Maithili
    • Maithili is one of the 22 scheduled languages of India as per the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
    • It is primarily spoken in the Indian state of Bihar and in parts of Nepal.
    • Maithili has a long literary history with significant contributions in poetry and folklore.
  • Awadhi
    • Awadhi is a dialect of the Eastern Hindi language group.
    • It is primarily spoken in the region of Awadh in Uttar Pradesh, India.
    • Awadhi has a rich tradition in literature, including works like the Ramcharitmanas by Tulsidas.
  • Braj
    • Braj is another dialect of the Western Hindi language group.
    • It is spoken mainly in the region of Braj Bhoomi, which includes parts of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.
    • Braj is known for its association with Lord Krishna and its contributions to Bhakti literature.

questions.question: Under the NPS Vatsalya Scheme Guidelines 2025, what is the minimum initial and annual contribution required to open and maintain an account for a minor?
questions.questionHtml: Under the NPS Vatsalya Scheme Guidelines 2025, what is the minimum initial and annual contribution required to open and maintain an account for a minor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ₹250.

In News

  • PFRDA issued the NPS Vatsalya Scheme Guidelines 2025, setting ₹250 as the minimum initial and annual contribution for minors.

Key Points

  • The minimum initial and annual contribution under NPS Vatsalya is ₹250.
  • The scheme is open to all Indian citizens including NRI and OCI below 18 years of age.
  • The account is opened in the name of the minor and operated by a guardian.
  • There is no maximum limit on the amount that can be contributed.

Additional Information

  • NPS Vatsalya
    • A contributory pension and savings scheme designed for minors
    • Allows early financial planning and long-term wealth creation
  • PFRDA
    • Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
    • The statutory regulator for the National Pension System in India
  • Transition on Attaining Majority
    • The account holder can continue in NPS Vatsalya or shift to NPS Tier I
    • Provides options for lump sum withdrawal and annuitisation
  • Financial Inclusion
    • Encourages saving habits from an early age
    • Supports the national vision of a financially secure society

questions.question: ___________ is set to host the first-ever Global Big Cat Summit in 2026, bringing together heads of governments and ministers from ______ range countries.
questions.questionHtml: ___________ is set to host the first-ever Global Big Cat Summit in 2026, bringing together heads of governments and ministers from ______ range countries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is India – 95.

In News

  • India will host the first-ever Global Big Cat Summit in 2026 to strengthen international cooperation for big cat conservation.

Key Points

  • India is the host of the first-ever Global Big Cat Summit.
  • The summit will bring together heads of governments and ministers from 95 range countries.
  • The announcement was made by Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during the Union Budget 2026–27.
  • The summit aims to strengthen global cooperation for the conservation of big cat species.

Additional Information

  • Global Big Cat Summit
    • Aims to create a global platform for coordinated conservation of big cat species.
    • Focuses on species such as tigers, lions, leopards, snow leopards, cheetahs, and jaguars.
  • International Big Cat Alliance
    • Established to facilitate collaboration among countries that are home to big cat species.
    • Supports conservation, protection, and sustainable management of big cats worldwide.
  • Big Cat Range Countries
    • Countries that are natural habitats of one or more big cat species.
    • Play a crucial role in global biodiversity and wildlife conservation efforts.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mary E. Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, and Shimon Sakaguchi.

In News

  • The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2025 was awarded to Mary E. Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, and Shimon Sakaguchi for their discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance.

Key Points

  • The award was given by the Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institutet.
  • The Nobel Prize recognizes significant contributions in fields like Medicine, Physics, Chemistry, Literature, Peace, and Economics.
  • The Nobel Prizes have been awarded since 1901 as per the will of Alfred Nobel, a Swedish chemist and inventor.
  • In 2023, the prize money for Nobel Laureates was around 11 million Swedish kronor (over 1 million US dollars).

Additional Information

  • Nobel Prizes
    • The Nobel Prizes are one of the world’s most prestigious awards, recognizing exceptional contributions to humanity.
    • The laureates receive a gold medal, a diploma, and a cash prize.
  • Peripheral Immune Tolerance
    • The discoveries by Brunkow, Ramsdell, and Sakaguchi have significantly advanced our understanding of immune regulation and tolerance in the body.
